events.text: Luoyang's peony fair fills every street with colour. A flower seller insists one bloom is worth a year's wages.

choices.text: Buy a cheap one for your room

effects.log: It dies in a week. The week is lovely.
You overhear three sect secrets and one marriage proposal. The murim gossips like anyone else.

events.text: Pilgrims climb the thousand steps to the Shaolin Temple on Mount Song. A monk sweeps the top step and never seems to finish.

effects.log: At the top the monk hands you the broom. You sweep until sunset. Nobody explains.

choices.text: Ask the monk why he sweeps

effects.log: 'The step is clean,' he says. 'I am not.' You think about it on the way down.

events.text: The Yellow River rises again. Farmers pile sandbags along the dike and look at every passer-by with hope.

effects.log: The dike holds. A grandmother brings you congee and calls you her favourite relative, just in case.
You hear the next day that it held. You tell yourself it would have anyway.

events.text: Kaifeng's night market: fried dough, fortune tellers, shadow puppets and a man selling 'genuine Heavenly Demon hair'.

effects.log: Seven kinds of dumpling. You regret nothing.
The play is about the Sword Saint. The puppet sword breaks. The children cheer anyway.

events.text: Recruiters from three sects set up tables in the market square, each loudly insulting the other two.

effects.log: You learn more about each sect from its rivals than from itself.
The crowd laughs. One recruiter writes your name down, not in a friendly way.

events.text: Ploughing a field near an old battlefield, a farmer turns up rusted spearheads by the dozen. He offers you one.

choices.text: Take one and ask its story

effects.log: 'Two hundred years ago,' he says, 'the sects fought the Cult here for nine days.' You hold the rust a long time.

choices.text: Help him plough around the dead

effects.log: It takes all day. You say a word for each skull you rebury.

events.text: A travelling judge sets up court under a locust tree. Today's case: two brothers, one ox, and a very long grudge.

ok.log: You split the ox's work by season. Both brothers think they won.

fail.log: Both brothers turn on you. The ox looks relieved.

effects.log: The judge is slow, fair and very bored. You learn something about patience.

events.text: A rickety bridge on the Central Plains road has a new tollkeeper: a bandit in a borrowed official's hat.

ok.log: He runs. The villagers keep the hat as a trophy.

fail.log: He is better than his hat. You pay double.

effects.log: Two taels. He writes you a receipt. It is spelled wrong.

events.text: Spring rain on the Central Plains, soft enough to walk in. The whole county smells of wet earth.

effects.log: Every drop is a lesson in timing. You get very wet and a little better.

choices.text: Sit under the eaves with tea

effects.log: You watch the rain for an hour and feel your heart slow down.

events.text: Soldiers close the imperial road for a prince's procession. Travellers wait in the ditch for half a day.

effects.log: The prince waves from his sedan chair. You wave back. It is the high point of his day, probably.
The goat path is steep and full of goats. You arrive first anyway.

events.text: In a Zhengzhou teahouse, two scholars argue whether the Orthodox sects are better than the Demonic Cult, or just better dressed.

effects.log: You argue well. A Cult spy in the corner writes it all down.
The whole teahouse laughs. The scholars buy you tea to stop you talking.

events.text: The temple fair of the City God: acrobats, fortune sticks, candied hawthorn and a strongman who challenges all comers.

ok.log: You lift him off the ground. The crowd throws coins. (15 taels)

fail.log: He folds you like laundry. The crowd throws sympathy.

effects.log: Stick forty-one: 'The patient crane catches the fish.' You decide it means you.

events.text: On the road below Mount Hua, an old pilgrim asks you to carry her bundle up the plank path on the cliff.

choices.text: Carry it up the cliff path

ok.log: The planks creak, the drop is endless, and she chats the whole way. At the top she presses a peach into your hand.

fail.log: Halfway up your knees shake so badly she carries the bundle and you.

effects.log: You pay a porter. She blesses you nine times.

events.text: A grain merchant in the Central Plains is buying up every sack before the harvest tax is announced.

effects.log: They hold their grain. The merchant loses a fortune and learns your face.
The tax is announced. Grain triples. So does your stake. (40 taels)

events.text: The Inn of the Crossroads is where the murim's news is born. Tonight a masked woman is buying drinks for everyone.

effects.log: She is from the Beggars' Union, and she is recruiting ears. You hear three rumours worth silver.
Something happens. You hear about it the next day, and are glad to have left.

events.text: The rain has not come for sixty days. The village drags the Dragon King's statue into the sun to shame him.

effects.log: It rains three days later. The village credits you personally.
Less divine, more useful. The ditch still carries water ten years later.

events.text: A wanted poster on the Central Plains road shows a face very like yours. The crime is 'excessive heroism in a restricted area'.

effects.log: A constable sees you do it. It becomes a very long afternoon.
The poster now shows someone with a magnificent moustache. Nobody ever looks twice at you again.

events.text: A forest of stone steles stands outside the old capital, carved with the calligraphy of emperors and swordsmen.

effects.log: The characters are sword forms in disguise. You leave with sore eyes and new ideas.

choices.text: Take a rubbing for your wall

effects.log: It costs you a morning and a little ink. It hangs in your room for years.

events.text: A Shaolin monk begging for alms on the road turns out to be the most dangerous man in the county. He is still very polite.

effects.log: He blesses you, eats it, and fixes your stance with one finger as he leaves.
'Give first,' he says. You do. The lesson is: give first.

events.text: On the Yellow River ferry, two men play dice and lose on purpose to lure in fools. They look at you.

effects.log: The passengers throw the dice into the river, and then the men. The ferryman does not stop for them.
A young farmer loses his seed money. You see his face the whole crossing.

events.text: Someone is stealing pears from a widow's orchard every night. She asks the strongest-looking passer-by to keep watch.

effects.log: The thieves are three monkeys from the hills. You share the pears with them. The widow laughs for a week.

ok.log: You catch a monkey by the tail. It bites you. The widow gives you a basket of pears for the effort.

fail.log: You fall out of the pear tree. The monkeys applaud.

events.text: The winter market sells frozen persimmons, sheepskin coats and hot wine by the ladle.

effects.log: Warm all winter. You look like a sheep. You do not care.

choices.text: Drink hot ginger tea with the traders

effects.log: By sunset you know the price of everything from here to the western passes.

events.text: A great sect parades through the city on its founding day, a hundred disciples in white robes, not one out of step.

effects.log: You see how they breathe together. It is a lesson in itself.
A young disciple at the back grins at you and nearly trips. Worth it.

events.text: In a ruined courtyard stands a well that locals say grants wisdom to anyone who drinks from it at midnight.

effects.log: It tastes like well water. You feel exactly as wise as before, which is to say, a little.

choices.text: Drop a coin and make a wish

effects.log: You wish for something you will never tell anyone. You feel better anyway.

events.text: Two sects claim the same mountain spring. Their disciples glare across it every morning, buckets in hand.

ok.log: A schedule: odd days, even days. It holds for a generation.

fail.log: Both sides tell you to mind your business, in stereo.

choices.text: Drink from it before either side can

effects.log: Everyone stares. It is excellent water.

events.text: A blind storyteller in the square tells the tale of the last war against the Cult. He gets the numbers right, and the names.

effects.log: He finishes with a name you know: someone who died at the Iron Gate. The crowd is silent.

choices.text: Pay him and ask for a love story

effects.log: He tells one about a swordsman and a physician. Everyone cries.

events.text: A summer so hot the dogs sleep in the wells. Tempers are short and so are the harvests.

effects.log: Slow progress, no heatstroke. Sensible.

choices.text: Train at noon to toughen up

effects.log: You collapse in the yard. The heat wins this round.

events.text: A retired general on the Central Plains is looking for a tutor in swordsmanship for his clumsy grandson.

choices.text: Take the job for a season

ok.log: The grandson improves from terrible to bad. The general pays well. (40 taels)

fail.log: The grandson cuts his own sleeve off. The general thanks you for trying. (10 taels)

effects.log: You send a friend. The friend sends you a jar of wine in thanks.

events.text: Rich young men from the capital tour the ruins of a destroyed sect, laughing and carving their names on the walls.

choices.text: Tell them whose walls these are

effects.log: One of them listens. The others laugh. The one who listened comes back later to scrub the names off.

ok.log: They leave, faster than they came.

fail.log: Their bodyguards were nearby. You leave instead.

events.text: A cloud of locusts darkens the sky over the fields. The villagers bang pots and wave torches.

effects.log: It does nothing to the locusts and a great deal for morale.
You carry the seed grain to the temple cellar. Next spring, the village can plant.

events.text: At the great crossroads of the Central Plains, a stone marker points four ways. Someone has scratched 'adventure' on the western side.

effects.log: You watch travellers choose their roads. Everyone hesitates for exactly the same number of breaths.

choices.text: Scratch your own word on it

effects.log: You scratch 'home' on the eastern side. Someone will need it.

events.text: The great bell of a Central Plains monastery has cracked, and the monks need a hundred strong backs to hang the new one.

effects.log: It takes three days and a great deal of shouting. When it rings, every village for ten li stops to listen.
Your name is carved on the inside of the bell, where only the bell can see it.

events.text: The road to the capital is packed with scholars going to the imperial exam, each carrying a basket of books and dread.

effects.log: Twelve scholars, one fire, a great deal of anxious poetry. You learn some of it.
Scholars will pay anything the night before an exam. (12 taels)

events.text: A garden in the old capital has a round moon gate. They say lovers who pass through it together never part.

effects.log: The gardener shakes his head at you. You shake yours back.
An old couple walks through, very slowly, holding hands. You understand the gate completely.

events.text: An herbalist in the hills pays well for mountain ginseng, and badly for anything else.

ok.log: A root the length of your hand. The herbalist pays thirty taels and asks where. You smile.

fail.log: Three days of mud and one angry badger.

choices.text: Learn the herbs from him instead

effects.log: He teaches you ten plants that heal and three that kill. You remember all thirteen.

events.text: A seven-storey pagoda nobody climbs any more. At night a single lamp burns at the top.

ok.log: An old nun keeps the lamp lit for her dead sect. She gives you tea and a blessing.

fail.log: The stairs give way on the fifth floor. You climb down with a sprained ankle and a strong opinion about pagodas.

choices.text: Leave the lamp to its keeper

effects.log: Some lights are not yours to visit.

events.text: Two escort agencies brawl over a crossroads inn's last room. Chairs fly. The innkeeper hides behind you.

ok.log: Both agencies stop to stare at you, then share the room. The innkeeper gives you his best one free.

fail.log: Both agencies turn on you, then share the room.

effects.log: The horse snores. It is still better than the inn tonight.

events.text: You walk the old capital's walls at sunset. From here you can see forty li of fields and a hundred smoking chimneys.

choices.text: Stay until the stars come out

effects.log: For a moment the whole empire looks peaceful. It is not, but the moment is real.
Twelve li at a run. The guards bet on whether you will finish. You do.
